common_name: Cascade Jewel Huckleberry (OSU Tetraploid Evergreen Huckleberry Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock propagated from cuttings in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this patented tetraploid selection (PP35,894, cultivar '124OSU') is vegetatively propagated and does not come true from seed.

directions: Cascade Jewel is an Oregon State University release bred by Ryan Contreras for a more structured, upright habit and thicker, more rigid stems than wild evergreen huckleberry, with eye-catching deep red new growth maturing to glossy dark green. Extremely floriferous, it produces pendulous racemes of white urn-shaped flowers in spring followed by medium-to-large, shiny purple-black berries with a sweet-tart, wild-forest flavor that ripen in late summer. Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) with organic mulch; the plant is notably drought- and salt-tolerant once established compared with the species. Like its wild parent it tolerates shade but fruits most heavily in full sun to partial shade.
